newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar seen moving narrowly in Asia.
newsitem.headline: Dollar seen moving narrowly in Asia.

text.p: The dollar is likely to hover in a narrow range against the yen in directionless Asian trade on Thursday due to a lack of fresh incentives.
The greenback is also expected to move narrowly versus the mark as operators are cautious ahead of the Bundesbank council meeting later on Thursday, traders said.
The Bank of Japan (BOJ) will release its quarterly economic report at 2.30 p.m. (0530 GMT), but traders do not expect the report to have a significant impact on the forex market.
"People are now more focused on the European situation than Japanese economic fundamentals," a trust bank trader said.

Position-squaring of mark shorts ahead of the Buba council meeting could help underpin the German currency in Asia, but downward pressure on the mark remains intact due to expectations that a future single European currency will be weak and broad-based, traders said.
"If we see buy-backs in mark/yen, the dollar/yen is also likely to be firmer. Support near 115 yen is looking solid for the dollar/yen," said a city bank trader.
The greenback is likely to be supported near 115 yen by buying interest from institutional investors and trust banks, traders said.
Meanwhile, Japanese exporters are not expected to sell dollars aggressively below 116 yen, traders said.
"The dollar is likely to remain stuck in a 115 to 117 yen range. There is nothing in sight that could push it out of this band," said the trust bank trader.
In Wednesday's New York trade, the dollar/yen ended higher but the dollar/mark's rally was cut short after setting a new 71-month high of 1.8325 marks in Europe.
The greenback came under some pressure overnight after Federal Reserve vice chairwoman Alice Rivlin said the dollar may not get much stronger.

Rivlin told the House Banking committee in testimony on Wednesday that the strength of the dollar had helped to keep import prices in check but that the currency was unlikely to race ahead much further.
